items.zh: 说好这顿我请，你怎么又偷偷把单买了？
items.scene: 朋友聚餐后你发现对方抢先结了账

answers.en: I said this one was on me — why'd you go behind my back and pay?
answers.note: 带埋怨，'go behind my back'指背着你动手，适合关系近、可以直说的朋友。

answers.en: We agreed I was treating. Why did you pay instead?
answers.note: 语气克制、就事论事，像认真讲道理，适合不想把气氛搞僵的场合。

answers.en: Come on, I told you dinner was my treat. Why'd you pay?
answers.note: 'Come on'带无奈，像半开玩笑地抗议，适合熟人之间不伤和气地抱怨。

items.zh: 周末来我家吃饭吧？我下厨，你有空吗？
items.scene: 你想请关系不错的同事来家里聚聚

answers.en: Come over for dinner this weekend? I'm cooking — you free?
answers.note: 最随意的邀约，'Come over'像顺口一说，适合已经很熟的朋友。

answers.en: Would you like to come to my place for dinner this weekend? I'll be cooking.
answers.note: 完整客气，给对方留足拒绝空间，适合关系还不太近或想显郑重时。

answers.en: How about dinner at my place this weekend? I'll cook.
answers.note: 用'How about'提建议，轻松又不失礼，适合普通同事。

items.zh: 你想吃什么？我来订位子。
items.scene: 你打算请客，提前问对方想吃什么

answers.en: What are you in the mood for? I'll book a table.
answers.note: 'in the mood for'问当下想吃什么，轻松口语，适合朋友之间。

answers.en: What kind of food would you like? I'll make a reservation.
answers.note: 'would you like'加'make a reservation'偏正式，适合请客户或长辈。

answers.en: Any preference? I'll grab us a table.
answers.note: 'Any preference'简短，'grab a table'随意，适合同事间快速定下来。

items.zh: 菜单给你，你看看想吃哪个？
items.scene: 刚坐下，你把菜单推给对面的朋友

answers.en: Here's the menu — see anything you like?
answers.note: 随口一问，把选择权交给对方，适合熟人聚餐。

answers.en: Would you like to take a look and pick something?
answers.note: 说法完整客气，给对方时间慢慢挑，适合请客或对方是长辈时。

answers.en: Take a look — what are you getting?
answers.note: 'what are you getting'是问对方点什么，像同辈各点各的，气氛轻松。

items.zh: 这个菜辣不辣？我怕太辣。
items.scene: 看菜单拿不准辣度，你问旁边的服务员

answers.en: Is this spicy?
answers.note: 最直接的问法，只想知道有没有辣，适合随便问问。

answers.en: How spicy is this dish?
answers.note: 问的是辣的程度，适合你能吃一点辣但怕太辣时。

answers.en: Does this have much heat to it?
answers.note: 'heat'指辣度，说法偏内行，适合确认这菜辣得凶不凶。

items.zh: 要不要再加个青菜？光吃肉不行。
items.scene: 桌上全是荤菜，你想再点一道素菜

answers.en: Should we add a veggie dish? We can't just eat meat.
answers.note: 直接提议，'veggie'口语，适合朋友之间。

answers.en: How about ordering some greens? All this meat isn't great.
answers.note: 'greens'指绿叶菜，语气委婉，像关心健康的建议。

answers.en: Maybe we should get a vegetable too — that's a lot of meat.
answers.note: 'Maybe'开头把话说软，还带理由，适合对长辈或不熟的人提。

items.zh: 来来来，咱俩走一个？
items.scene: 公司聚餐，你想跟旁边的同事碰一杯

answers.en: Come on, let's do a shot, you and me.
answers.note: 'do a shot'指干一小杯烈酒，随意热闹，适合同辈拼酒。

answers.en: How about a toast — just us two?
answers.note: 'a toast'是举杯致意，不一定干杯，比'shot'斯文。

answers.en: Why don't we have a drink together?
answers.note: 用'Why don't we'提出，客气不劝酒，适合不太熟或不想喝多时。

items.zh: 你开车来的？那以茶代酒行不行？
items.scene: 聚餐发现同事开了车，你想敬他

answers.en: You drove here, right? Then let's skip the alcohol — I'll toast you with tea.
answers.note: 把理由说全，语气体贴，适合照顾开车来的同事。

answers.en: You're driving, so no booze for you. Tea toast?
answers.note: 'no booze'直爽，'Tea toast?'省略俏皮，适合熟人。

answers.en: Since you're driving, how about we toast with tea instead?
answers.note: 'Since'先摆理由，'how about'商量口吻，适合正式一点的饭局。

items.zh: 你坐里面还是外面？
items.scene: 两人进餐厅，服务员领到靠墙的卡座

answers.en: Do you want the inside or the outside?
answers.note: 最直白，把两个位置摆出来让对方挑，适合熟人。

answers.en: Would you prefer the seat against the wall or the one on the aisle?
answers.note: 说得具体又客气，适合约会或对方是长辈，显得周到。

answers.en: Inside or outside — which works for you?
answers.note: 先抛两个选项再问，节奏快，适合关系随意、不想客套时。

items.zh: 主位留给王总，咱们坐这边行吗？
items.scene: 商务饭局上，你安排同事入座

answers.en: Let's save the head seat for Mr. Wang. Can we sit over here?
answers.note: 'head seat'指主位，说法正式，适合商务场合。

answers.en: The seat at the head is for Mr. Wang — you mind sitting this side?
answers.note: 用'you mind'征求意见，客气，适合同事之间。

answers.en: Mr. Wang gets the head of the table. We'll take these seats, okay?
answers.note: 直接安排再补一句'okay'，干脆不失礼，适合你负责张罗时。

items.zh: 你吃不吃辣？我点菜好有个数。
items.scene: 点菜前你问第一次一起吃饭的新同事

answers.en: Do you eat spicy food?
answers.note: 中性询问，只问吃不吃，不带假设，适合初次一起吃饭。

answers.en: Can you handle spicy food?
answers.note: 'handle'暗示能不能扛住辣，略带挑战，适合朋友间打趣。

answers.en: Are you okay with spicy?
answers.note: 简短随意，'okay with'问能否接受，适合边看菜单边问。

items.zh: 你口味重不重？这家店偏咸。
items.scene: 推荐餐厅时提醒朋友这家菜偏咸

answers.en: Do you like your food on the salty side? This place leans salty.
answers.note: 'on the salty side'形容偏咸，说法形象，适合闲聊推荐。

answers.en: How do you feel about strong flavors? This place runs salty.
answers.note: 'strong flavors'指味重，'runs salty'指一贯偏咸，适合介绍特色。

answers.en: Are you big on flavor? This place goes heavy on salt.
answers.note: 'big on'是喜欢、看重，'goes heavy on'指下手重，口语感强，适合熟人。

items.zh: 香菜你能接受吗？
items.scene: 点菜时你想确认对方吃不吃香菜

answers.en: Are you okay with cilantro?
answers.note: 'cilantro'是美式说法，'okay with'问能否接受，最中性。

answers.en: Do you do cilantro?
answers.note: 'Do you do...'是口语问吃不吃某物，简短，适合年轻人。

answers.en: Is cilantro a dealbreaker for you?
answers.note: 'dealbreaker'夸张指完全不能接受，带玩笑味，适合朋友间。

items.zh: 你有什么忌口吗？
items.scene: 请客户吃饭，点菜前你礼貌问一句

answers.en: Is there anything you don't eat?
answers.note: 直白清楚，不追问原因，适合大多数场合，也不显得冒犯。

answers.en: Any dietary restrictions I should know about?
answers.note: 'dietary restrictions'涵盖过敏和宗教禁忌，正式，适合商务宴请。

answers.en: Anything you can't have?
answers.note: 简短省事，'can't have'指不能吃，适合已经比较熟时。

items.zh: 你不吃牛肉对吧？那这个菜换掉吧？
items.scene: 你记得朋友不吃牛肉，正要点牛肉菜

answers.en: You don't eat beef, right? Let's swap this dish out.
answers.note: 先确认再提议，'swap out'指换掉，语气自然。

answers.en: You steer clear of beef, don't you? I'll pick something else.
answers.note: 'steer clear of'是避开，说法委婉，不想显得冒犯时用。

answers.en: Beef's off the table for you, isn't it? I'll order something different.
answers.note: 'off the table'双关又轻松，适合熟人之间开玩笑。

items.zh: 服务员，能买单吗？
items.scene: 吃完想结账，你朝服务员招手

answers.en: Could we get the check, please?
answers.note: 美式餐厅标准说法，'check'即账单，礼貌通用。

answers.en: Check, please.
answers.note: 极简，招手时喊一句就行，适合嘈杂的餐厅。

answers.en: Could we settle up?
answers.note: 'settle up'指结清账目，干脆利落，适合小馆子或熟店。

items.zh: 咱俩AA还是我请？
items.scene: 同事午饭吃完，你掏出手机准备付钱

answers.en: Should we split it or is this on me?
answers.note: 'split it'指平摊，'on me'指我请，两个选项并列，最常用。

answers.en: Do you want to go Dutch or should I get it?
answers.note: 'go Dutch'是各付各的，稍老派但清楚，适合普通同事。

answers.en: I've got this — or do you want to split?
answers.note: 先说自己付再给台阶，语气主动，适合不想让对方为难时。

items.zh: 这顿多少钱？我转你。
items.scene: 朋友先垫了钱，散场时你问

answers.en: How much was dinner? Let me pay you back.
answers.note: 'pay you back'指还钱，说法通用，适合朋友之间。

answers.en: What do I owe you for dinner?
answers.note: 'What do I owe you'最自然地问该给多少，语气客气。

answers.en: How much was my share? I'll send it over.
answers.note: 'my share'强调自己那份，'send it over'指转账，适合AA。

items.zh: 上次你请的，这次该我了吧？
items.scene: 朋友又抢着买单，你按住他的手

answers.en: You got it last time — my turn, right?
answers.note: 'got it'指付了钱，'my turn'轻松提醒轮到自己，适合熟人。

answers.en: You paid last time. Let me get this one.
answers.note: 陈述加请求，语气平和坚定，适合不想推来推去时。

answers.en: It's my turn to treat, isn't it?
answers.note: 用反义疑问句，带商量和坚持，适合关系一般时委婉争取。

items.zh: 这些剩的能打包吗？
items.scene: 聚餐结束，桌上还剩不少菜

answers.en: Could we get a box for the leftovers?
answers.note: 'a box'是美式餐厅要打包盒的常用说法，适合大多数餐厅。

answers.en: Can we take the rest to go?
answers.note: 'to go'指带走，说法简洁，适合快餐或休闲餐厅。

answers.en: Could you pack up what's left, please?
answers.note: 'pack up'请服务员帮忙装，语气客气，适合正式餐厅。

items.zh: 这些你带回去给孩子吃吧？
items.scene: 散场时你把没动过的菜推给朋友

answers.en: Take these home for your kid, okay?
answers.note: 直接又亲切，'kid'口语，适合关系好的朋友。

answers.en: Why don't you take the leftovers home for your child?
answers.note: 用'Why don't you'委婉建议，适合不太熟时。

answers.en: Bring these back for your kid — they're barely touched.
answers.note: 补一句没怎么动过打消顾虑，说法体贴，适合熟人。

items.zh: 路上堵车，我可能晚到十分钟，你们先点？
items.scene: 聚餐快开始，你被堵在路上发消息

answers.en: Stuck in traffic — I'll be about ten minutes late. Go ahead and order?
answers.note: 省略主语像发消息，节奏快，适合微信群随口说。

answers.en: I'm running about ten minutes behind because of traffic. Start without me?
answers.note: 'running behind'指比计划晚，说法清楚，适合正式一点的约。

answers.en: Traffic's bad, so I may be ten minutes late. Would you mind ordering first?
answers.note: 'Would you mind'客气，适合请客时怕耽误大家。

items.zh: 你们吃到哪儿了？我还得二十分钟。
items.scene: 你迟到很久，在群里问大家进度

answers.en: Where are you guys at with the food? I need another twenty minutes.
answers.note: 'Where are you at'问进度，口语随意，适合朋友群。

answers.en: How far along is dinner? I'm still twenty minutes out.
answers.note: 'how far along'问进展，'twenty minutes out'说还有多远，清楚。

answers.en: Have you started eating? I won't be there for another twenty minutes.
answers.note: 直接问加说明，语气平实，适合对长辈或客户。

items.zh: 下回该我请了，行吧？
items.scene: 吃完饭告别，你跟朋友约下次

answers.en: Next time it's on me, okay?
answers.note: 'on me'指我请，加'okay'半商量，轻松自然。

answers.en: I'll treat next time — deal?
answers.note: 'deal?'像击掌约定，俏皮，适合关系好的朋友。

answers.en: Let me host next time, all right?
answers.note: 'host'偏正式，指做东，适合请客对象是同事或长辈。

items.zh: 下次还来这家吗？
items.scene: 吃完走出餐厅，你回头看了眼招牌

answers.en: Should we come back here next time?
answers.note: 'come back'指再来，语气商量，适合常一起吃饭的同伴。

answers.en: Wanna hit this place again next time?
answers.note: 'Wanna hit'非常随意，像年轻人约饭，适合好朋友。

answers.en: Would you come back here again?
answers.note: 问对方意愿，措辞平和，适合约会或不熟的人。
